title: Poland Observes National Mourning After Krakow Square Shooting
dek: Sunday and Monday are days of national mourning after six people were killed in Krakow; investigators are examining the attacker's motives and the deaths at his home.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Aerial-style view of Kraków's Main Market Square with the St. Mary's Basilica and historic buildings

keyPoints: President Karol Nawrocki signed a regulation declaring Nov. 8 and 9 national days of mourning, per Poland's state news agency PAP.
Six people were killed in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday; police said the victims included a British national.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the attack terrorism and said police are investigating all of its circumstances.
Tusk said two more women and one man were found dead at the suspect's home, most likely members of his family.
body:
Poland is observing two days of national mourning, Sunday, Nov. 8, and Monday, Nov. 9, after a gunman opened fire in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon. President Karol Nawrocki signed a regulation on Saturday night declaring the two days, according to PAP.

## The attack and the toll

Police said the gunman fired from a vehicle in the square shortly after 3 p.m. local time. Four women and two men were killed, three of them Polish women and one a British national, Polish police said; two of the victims had not been identified at the time of the police briefing. Tusk later said two more women and one man were found dead at the suspect's home, most likely members of his family.

Reports on the number of injured vary. The Guardian's live coverage counted 16 injured, including the suspect; AP reported 15 others wounded. Two police officers were shot in the exchange of fire, one in serious condition. Several foreign nationals were among the wounded.

## What authorities say about the suspect

The suspect is a Polish citizen. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said he held "very radical" and "ultra-nationalistic" views, and authorities are evaluating reports that he was fixated on far-right ideology. Reports differ on his age: AP gave it as 24, while the Guardian gave it as 25. Police said he was dressed in military-style clothing and used a long military-type firearm.

## The investigation

Tusk said police are examining all circumstances of the attack and the motives behind it, and he warned against disinformation circulating online. Poland's defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, called it an act of terror. Police chief inspector Marek Boroń said armed officers responded within three minutes of the first report.

## What remains unknown

Officials had not released a full list of the victims' names as of the latest reporting. Investigators have not publicly confirmed a complete account of the attacker's motives, and the reporting cited here does not establish any link to organized groups.
